Out-of-pocket expense limits</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>a. Network</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Network services are subject to the same limits described below for non-network services.</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>b. Non-network</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>When a covered person&#x27;s out-of-pocket expenses reach $2,000 in any year, any further benefits that would have been paid at 60%, 80%, 90%, or 95% will be paid at 100% of usual and customary charges for the remainder of that year, to the maximum benefit amounts.</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'></td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>c. Expenses that do not count toward the individual</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>When two or more family members satisfy their deductibles and have combined out-of-pocket expenses of $4,000 (but not more than $2,000 for any one individual), any further benefits that would have been paid at 60%, 70%, 80%, 90%, or 95% will be paid at 100% of usual and customary charges for the remainder of that year, to the maximum benefit amounts.</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'></td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>d. Expenses that do not count toward the individual</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>1) Yearly deductibles. 2) Hospital emergency room co-payment. 3) Office visit co-payment.</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Varies by plan.</td></tr></table>

c. Expenses that do not count toward the individual or family out-of-pocket expense limits

4) Difference between usual and customary charges and the provider's actual charge.
